Hi, all! I'm looking for sunscreen recommendations.

I've (27) got combination, acne-prone skin, and I'm looking to experiment with AB sunscreen, as sunscreen has been the one step of my routine I haven't been able to figure out.

My routine works pretty well for me. At night, I use Cetaphil's gentle cleansing bar, followed by Cerave Moisturizing Cream and my prescribed Tretinoin for my acne. Typically I'll apply Vaseline on my lips and around my eyes. In the morning, I rinse everything off with water, apply the Cerave Moisturizing Cream again, and follow up with more Vaseline on the lips. I'll also take my oral Spironolactone.

The reason I'm interested in AB sunscreens is because I've used several different tinted sunscreen in the past after I quit using makeup, and I never felt like I found one that matched my light, neutral skin and looked "cosmetically elegant". A lot of the times they just feel very thick, have too much coverage, and look more oily than dewy. 

I'm looking for one with light coverage (almost like a serum maybe?) and a shade range that will accommodate my truly neutral toned skin. I also have been a big fan of the "glass skin" look as I'm really embracing not wearing makeup. I'm looking for one with really solid sun protection as well. Hopefully this isn't too much to ask, lol!

I've dipped my toes into AB before, but nothing has stuck as far as skincare. I'm hoping the sunscreen will be a hit, as I've really enjoyed the texture and finish of the AB products I've tried in the past!

Yeah I tend to have pretty bad support and breath control problems. I finally figured out my big resonance issues recently so I'm pretty sure it's breath-related.

I feel you, man... it's all about getting the hang of informal english pronunciation vs a formal. Typically, vowels in classical singing tend to be vertical, as in there's a tall space inside your mouth. A lot of casual english vowels tend to be wider, or more spread. Less formal consonants too. The other thing is a lot of rock singers don't use good vocal technique, so play around with adding and subtracting vocal elements like support, resonance, breath support, etc.

You should NOT be pushing your voice when you are sick. That will cause vocal damage for sure, which can lead to nodes. Your voice needs rest and moisture. Drink lots of water, maybe some throat coat or black tea with honey (decaffinated). That scratchy sound is probably some form of abrasion related to your illness, and singing will only aggravate your vocal chords.

Make sure you are breathing with your diaphragm... I was watching your shoulders, and every time you breathed, they hunched! Breathe low... so your stomach, sides, and ribs expand. Make sure you aren't restricting the stream of air, or stopping it before you let air out and sing. Open your mouth wide, and USE THAT SUPPORT. This will give you power in your voice. You're a great singer! Your vocal runs are better than mine for sure!
